title: Guarded step-lattice with shadow probing for canary rollouts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a canary rollout configuration and policy engine that treats rollout steps as a directed lattice of guarded states and includes lightweight shadow probing. The lattice allows non-linear step transitions (split increases, temporary holds, lateral probes) with explicit guard evaluations (latency, error rate, quality regressions). Shadow probing runs a configurable fraction of traffic to the new variant without affecting responses, enabling signal fusion for safety decisions. The goal is to reduce blast radius of bad model updates while enabling faster safe rollouts for predictable workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Can express rollout as a step-lattice where nodes define traffic split, hold conditions, and probe actions
Configuration DSL validates and compiles to runtime directives accepted by the router
Shadow probe paths can be enabled per-route with independent sampling rates and per-probe timeouts
Guard evaluation supports composite conditions: latency P95 disparity, error-rate delta, Quality metric (from evals) drop > threshold
Automatic rollback triggers when any critical guard crosses a threshold for the configured evaluation window
End-to-end integration test demonstrating a safe canary increase, hold, lateral probe, and auto-rollback in staging
design_notes: Represent rollout steps as nodes in a DAG rather than a strict list to allow branching (A/B forks) and lateral experiments
Guards evaluate over sliding windows (default 5m, configurable) and support both absolute and delta thresholds
Shadow probing relies on asynchronous fanout: primary response path returns nothing from shadow, but probe observes full model output for offline scoring
Runtime must surface per-route probe metrics to Console with a dedicated probe dashboard and make those metrics addressable in guard expressions
Keep the DSL minimal: step ::= {id, traffic_percent, guards, probes, next: [ids], rollback_on_fail: bool}
implementation_plan: Draft DSL schema and compile unit (stage 1) — 2w
Extend router to accept step-lattice directives and shadow probe config (stage 2) — 3w
Instrumentation: probe collectors and metric pipeline tags for probe-run ids (stage 3) — 1.5w
Policy evaluator service: evaluate guards and emit state transitions + webhook hooks (stage 4) — 2w
E2E tests and staging rollout demonstrating rollback (stage 5) — 1w
Docs + Console surface for probe dashboard and lattices (parallel)
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser and validator
Property tests for lattice compilation to ensure no unreachable nodes
Load tests: router with shadow fanout at 10% probe rate for 1000 RPS target route
Chaos test: inject latency spikes in canary variant and verify guard triggers auto-rollback
Quality regression test: synthetic prompt set where canary returns lower quality score to ensure guard delta detection
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime-flag in staging and dedicated test orgs
Enable lattice config for a low-traffic demo route (1 RPS) with 10% shadow probing
Run 24-48h observational window, validate probe metrics map to guard metrics
Expand traffic for progressive test: 1% -> 5% -> 20% split following successful guard checks
Enable automatic rollback in staging to validate end-to-end
monitoring_and_guardrails: Primary SLOs observed: latency P50/P95, API error rate, token-level rejection rate
Probe-specific metrics: probe_latency_ms P95, probe_success_rate, probe_coverage (fraction of requests probed)
Guard expressions accessible in Console; default templates: latency-delta > 1.5x, error-rate-delta > 0.5%, quality-drop > 3%
A safety window after each step during which lateral probes are sampled more aggressively
Manual override endpoints (pause, force-promote, force-rollback) with audit logs
